key_insight: The paper shows that arbitrary 2D curves and simple 3D shapes can be deterministically drawn on water surfaces by superposing transient multi-directional focused waves with curve-based sampling and amplitude correction.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to precise wave-field shaping for ocean engineering, with potential use in testing, visualization, and controlled wave generation.
method: Parameterize target shapes with Bézier curves
Sample points by equal arc length to place wave foci uniformly
Use Iterative Amplitude Correction to reduce overshoot and improve superposition
evidence_signal: The approach was checked against linear wave theory and SPH simulations, then demonstrated experimentally in the FloWave basin for a 2D star and 3D pyramid.
watch_item: Accuracy may degrade for higher-amplitude waves, so nonlinear effects will need to be incorporated for robust real-world deployment.
